questions.stem: What three dimensions are combined in the triple bottom line?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The triple bottom line evaluates social, environmental, and economic performance together rather than treating them as unrelated.
incorrectOptionExplanations: These are management elements, not the sustainability framework.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 33, triple bottom line theory, pp. 749-750

questions.stem: A product uses less energy during operation but creates substantially more hazardous waste during manufacture and disposal. What is the best sustainability approach?
options: Ignore disposal because it occurs after sale
Compare impacts across the full lifecycle before declaring the product preferable
Choose the option with the lowest purchase price
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Lifecycle thinking considers raw materials, production, use, transport, maintenance, and end-of-life effects.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One lifecycle stage can shift impacts to another.
End-of-life effects remain part of the total environmental and social burden.
Purchase price alone does not represent lifecycle cost or impact.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 33, sustainable development and conservation principles, pp. 743-751

questions.stem: Which measure is the strongest sustainability KPI for a solvent-reduction program?
options: Total production volume without solvent data
Hazardous solvent use per unit of production with verified waste and exposure outcomes
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An intensity metric normalized to production and linked to waste and exposure shows whether source reduction is real and sustained.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Poster count measures activity, not material or risk performance.
Production alone cannot show whether solvent intensity improved.
One opinion is not a reliable outcome or trend measure.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 33, key performance indicators and economic benefits, pp. 749-751

questions.stem: Which initiative best reflects pollution prevention rather than end-of-pipe control?
options: Change the process so the pollutant is not generated
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Pollution prevention reduces or eliminates pollutants at the source before treatment, recycling, or disposal is needed.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Storage manages generated waste but does not prevent it.
Disposal transfers the material after generation.
Dilution does not reduce pollutant mass and may not be lawful.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 33 and 34, conservation and pollution prevention, pp. 743-778

questions.stem: Which action most directly supports the people dimension of sustainability in a major process change?
options: Engage affected workers, protect health, build competence, and assess community consequences
Select the cheapest supplier without labor or safety review
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Social sustainability includes health, equity, capability, participation, and effects on workers and communities.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Profit is one dimension and cannot represent worker and community outcomes.
Low price alone may hide serious social and safety impacts.
Operators provide essential task and exposure knowledge.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 33, sustainable development of society and conservation of human resources, pp. 746-749

questions.stem: A company advertises a product as sustainable based on one minor packaging change while withholding increased emissions. What is the main concern?
options: Every sustainability claim requires zero environmental impact
The claim is misleading because material negative impacts are omitted
Marketing claims are unrelated to professional ethics
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Credible sustainability communication uses complete, material evidence and does not exaggerate a narrow improvement.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Sustainability improvement does not require absolute zero impact, but claims must be accurate and balanced.
Packaging can affect material, transport, and waste impacts.
Safety professionals should communicate objectively and avoid deceptive statements.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 33, sustainability performance; Chapter 40, objective and truthful professional statements
